gap: No result ChatGPT got puts every Grandfalls model's rated working flow next to the bring-your-own-reel options. Giraffe's own spec tables, seen only in search snippets and not yet opened, give 1.2 GPM rated flow for the Plus, the G20 and (on the AU page) the Pro. If that holds, the $225–$595 Grandfalls models differ only in rated PSI, not in water flow, while the Kränzle K1322TS (1.9–1.97 GPM) and Giraffe's own Crossfalls Ultra (2.6 GPM, $949.99) move far more water.
standout_why: progaragegear.com (cited) lists only the advertised maximums: G20 2,500 PSI / 2.2 GPM, Plus 2,900 / 2.2, Pro 3,700 / 1.6, Kränzle 1.9 GPM. It already warns that 'Listed PSI and GPM are maximums and are not delivered together', and gives a real-world flow range only for the base Grandfalls. Bob Vila (cited) gives an unlabelled '3,700 PSI rating', no GPM and no measurements. ChatGPT's own answer already quoted rated figures (Pro 2,700 PSI / 1.2 GPM, Plus 2,100 / 1.2) and told shoppers to compare rated performance. That leaves only part of the normalisation as new: the same rated flow across the whole Grandfalls line, the Pro's conflicting rated PSI (2,500 on the AU page vs the 2,700 ChatGPT quoted), and the Crossfalls Ultra as a 2.6 GPM all-in-one that no rival or ChatGPT card mentions. I could not open Popular Mechanics or the Giraffe blog post (fetch blocked or truncated).
decides: If the rated 1.2 GPM is confirmed for every Grandfalls model, the Pro's extra $155–$370 over the Lite Pro, Plus or G20 buys rated pressure and an induction motor, not more rinse water. For car washing with a foam cannon (ChatGPT's 'detailing' branch), flow is what matters. That points to the Crossfalls Ultra (2.6 GPM, retractable, $949.99) as the all-in-one pick, ahead of the 'Active 2.3 + separate reel' build, and confirms the Kränzle + reel as the serviceable premium choice. For mixed driveway and car use, the cheaper Lite Pro or Plus match the Pro on rated flow.
